To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the percolation behavior of nanorodfilled polymer nanocomposites is affected by interfacial interaction and aspect ratio of fillers; the percolation mechanism of the nanorodfilled composites under shear is different from that under static condition; the evolution of conductive network is investigated under shear.
the percolation mechanism of nanorods filled polymer composites is influenced by the interfacial interactions, aspect ratios of the nanorods, external shear fields and temperature.

(1) the percolation thresholds of the nanorod-filled polymers can be tuned by interfacial interaction and filler morphology; (2) the percolated network can be controlled by an external shear field and temperature; (3) the conductivity of the nanorods is enhanced under shear.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conductive mechanism of polymer nanocomposites filled with nanorods.

the conductive properties of nanorod/polymer composites, and the effects of interfacial interactions between the fillers and the matrix, filler–filler interactions, the aspect ratio of the nanorods and temperature on the percolation behavior.
the conductivity mechanism of the nanorod filled polymeric nanocomposites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conductivity probability increases with the interfacial interactions and aspect ratio of the filler.
the percolation mechanism of the nanorod filled composites is strongly influenced by the interfacial interactions, aspect ratio, temperature, filler-filler interactions and external shear field.
the percolation mechanism of nanorods in polymer nanocomposites is strongly dependent on interfacial interactions, aspect ratios, shear field, filler–filler interaction, and temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the percolation behavior of conductive fillers is strongly dependent on interfacial interaction and the aspect ratio of the conductive fillers.

the interfacial interactions between fillers and polymer chains, the aspect ratio of fillers, the filler-filler interaction in the composites, the temperature and the external shear field are all important factors that can affect the conductivity mechanism in nanorod-filled composites.
the percolation mechanism of polymer composites can be understood from the viewpoint of the interfacially induced aggregation of the conductive fillers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the percolation thresholds of nanorod composites can be tuned by the interfacial interactions, aspect ratio of nanorods and temperature.
the conductivity mechanism of the nanorod filled nanocomposite can be controlled by adjusting the interfacial interactions and the aspect ratios of the nanorods.
the interfacial interactions play an important role in determining the conductivity mechanism of polymer nanocomposites.
